ValueError: RepairPlannerStopped: The requested repair cannot be completed with the available tool contracts, and fabricating a membership record would violate the no-invention rule. Precisely: HypergeometricEnrichment derives its term family only from the term_ids present in the membership file (file mode) or from the term_members dict (inline mode). To honor the immutable requirement 'BH over all six terms, including empty categories', all six GO IDs (GO:0005634, GO:0005737, GO:0005829, GO:0005886, GO:0005773, GO:0005811) must each appear as a term row. A term that has at least one eligible record (even for a gene outside the testable universe) will still be emitted with K=0, k=0, p=1 under ignore_report, so the only failing case is a declared term with ZERO non-negated, experimental-evidence annotation records anywhere in the snapshot. For that case the reviewer's 'explicit empty-term marker' record must be synthesized/merged into the membership file, but none of the four available contracts can do this: QueryScientificRecordsFile only filters/projects records that already exist; AdjustPValues only adjusts a p-value family; FitBulkRNASeqCounts only fits counts; HypergeometricEnrichment only reads a supplied membership. Inline mode is not a workaround because (a) the binding language has no object/dict constructor and cannot build dynamic term_members keys, and (b) the full testable universe (~14599 ids) exceeds the 10000-item inline limit and no node emits a full id array. Using the non-experimental-evidence records to force term presence would wrongly add non-experimental members and corrupt K/k, violating 'use only the declared experimental evidence set'. Therefore the six-term family (with empty categories) and the family_size=6 guarantee cannot be satisfied deterministically without either (1) confirmation from the snapshot that every one of the six GO IDs has ≥1 non-negated experimental-evidence record (in which case file-mode membership already yields family_size=6), or (2) a tool that can concatenate/merge record files or synthesize a controlled empty-term marker record. Neither is presently available, so I am returning stop rather than resubmitting an unsatisfiable family_size=6 check or inventing a membership row.

PlanningFailure: ValueError: PlannerStopped: Missing capability: a joint (pooled) multi-group proper-rigid fitter with class-preserving chain-bijection enumeration for two deposited PDB assemblies. The task needs, per allowed bijection, (a) the minimized summed squared residual of ONE shared proper rotation+translation fitted to all 4×27=108 corresponding CA points simultaneously, and (b) the minimized pooled SSE of four independent per-chain proper rigid fits (point-count weighted, no reflection, no scaling, no residue reassignment), plus total point counts, so that least_global_rmsd_angstrom = sqrt(SSE_global/108), least_independent_chain_pooled_rmsd_angstrom = sqrt(SSE_chain/108) and global_sse_fraction_removed_by_chainwise_fits = 1 - SSE_chain_min/SSE_global_min can be derived and minimized over the 4 bijections. What exists cannot supply this: ExtractPDBCoordinates returns one chain at a time (27 CA points, exact residue IDs, Biopython altloc policy), InspectPDBQuality can verify model 0, chains A,B,C,D, residue IDs and altlocs, but RigidSuperposition only performs PAIRWISE Kabsch fits between explicitly corresponding equal-length point sets (≤256 points each) and offers no way to concatenate the four 27-point chain arrays into a single 108-point set or to pool one shared transform across groups; ExecuteNumericalCode accepts only a literal code string (upstream node values cannot be injected into the source) and its sandbox forbids filesystem/network access, so it cannot read the PDB coordinates or receive the extracted arrays. Consequently the single-global-pose SSE over the whole four-chain cohort, the pooled chainwise SSE, and their nested-model fraction cannot be computed with the registered tools.
